import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.53

by D. J. S. Robinson

Is the isomorphism problem soluble for finitely presented soluble groups of
finite rank?

Here “finite rank” means finite Prüfer rank: there is a uniform finite bound on
the number of generators needed by every finitely generated subgroup.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.53»

/-- An encoded finite group presentation. A signed letter `(i, b)` refers to
the generator with index `i`; the Boolean records its sign. -/
structure FinitePresentation where
  generatorCount : ℕ
  relators : List (List (ℕ × Bool))
  deriving Encodable

namespace FinitePresentation

/-- Every generator index appearing in a presentation is in range. -/
def WellFormed (P : FinitePresentation) : Prop :=
  ∀ w ∈ P.relators, ∀ x ∈ w, x.1 < P.generatorCount

/-- Interpret a word in the free group on the presentation's generators.
Out-of-range letters are discarded; `WellFormed` excludes them in the promise
used by the conjecture. -/
def word (P : FinitePresentation) (w : List (ℕ × Bool)) :
    FreeGroup (Fin P.generatorCount) :=
  FreeGroup.mk <| w.filterMap fun x =>
    if h : x.1 < P.generatorCount then some (⟨x.1, h⟩, x.2) else none

/-- The set of relators represented by a finite presentation. -/
def relations (P : FinitePresentation) : Set (FreeGroup (Fin P.generatorCount)) :=
  word P '' {w | w ∈ P.relators}

/-- The group represented by a finite presentation. -/
def Group (P : FinitePresentation) : Type :=
  PresentedGroup P.relations

instance (P : FinitePresentation) : _root_.Group P.Group := by
  change _root_.Group (PresentedGroup P.relations)
  infer_instance

end FinitePresentation

/-- A group has finite Prüfer rank if some `r` uniformly bounds the number of
generators required by each of its finitely generated subgroups. -/
def HasFinitePrueferRank (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ r : ℕ, ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG →
    ∃ S : Finset H, S.card ≤ r ∧ Subgroup.closure (S : Set H) = ⊤

/-- The promise on an encoded presentation in Problem 9.53: it is well formed
and represents a soluble group of finite Prüfer rank. -/
def FinitePresentation.IsSolubleFiniteRank (P : FinitePresentation) : Prop :=
  P.WellFormed ∧ IsSolvable P.Group ∧ HasFinitePrueferRank P.Group

/--
Is the isomorphism problem soluble for finitely presented soluble groups of
finite rank?

Precisely, does there exist a computable predicate on pairs of encoded finite
presentations which correctly decides group isomorphism whenever both
presentations represent soluble groups of finite Prüfer rank? This is a promise
problem: the predicate is unconstrained on presentations outside that class.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.53» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ decideIsomorphic : ℕ → ℕ → Bool, Computable₂ decideIsomorphic ∧
      ∀ P Q : FinitePresentation,
        P.IsSolubleFiniteRank → Q.IsSolubleFiniteRank →
          (decideIsomorphic (Encodable.encode P) (Encodable.encode Q) = true ↔
            Nonempty (P.Group ≃* Q.Group)) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.53»
modeling_decisions: Finite presentations are encoded by a natural generator count and a finite list of relator words, with letters represented by a natural generator index and a Boolean sign.
Only well-formed presentation encodings are included in the promise; the interpretation of malformed words discards out-of-range letters, but this behavior cannot affect the promised inputs.
The presented group is Mathlib's `PresentedGroup` on the finite set of interpreted relators, so each listed relator is imposed as equal to the identity via normal closure.
Finite rank is interpreted as finite Prüfer rank: one natural number uniformly bounds the size of a generating set for every finitely generated subgroup.

The algorithm is a total `Computable₂` Boolean function on pairs of natural-number encodings. Its behavior is constrained only when both encoded presentations represent solvable groups of finite Prüfer rank.
Abstract group isomorphism is represented by `Nonempty (P.Group ≃* Q.Group)`.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.53

by D. J. S. Robinson

Is the isomorphism problem soluble for finitely presented soluble groups of finite rank?

Here "soluble" applied to the isomorphism problem means decidable: there is an algorithm
which, given two finite presentations of groups in the class, halts and decides whether the
two presented groups are isomorphic. Membership in the class is not decidable, so this is a
promise problem: on pairs of finite presentations that do not both present soluble (solvable)
groups of finite rank the algorithm may answer arbitrarily or fail to halt.

A group has *finite rank* (in the sense of Prüfer and Mal'cev) if there is an integer $r$
such that every finitely generated subgroup can be generated by $r$ elements.

A finite presentation $\langle x_0, \dots, x_{n-1} \mid R \rangle$ is encoded by the number
$n$ of generators together with a finite list of relators, each a word in the letters
$x_i^{\pm 1}$. An algorithm is a partial recursive function (`Partrec₂`) on these encodings.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.53»

/-- A finite group presentation $\langle x_0, \dots, x_{n-1} \mid R \rangle$.
A letter `(i, b)` of a relator stands for $x_i$ if `b = true` and for $x_i^{-1}$ if
`b = false`. -/
structure FinitePresentation where
  /-- The number $n$ of generators $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$. -/
  numGenerators : ℕ
  /-- The finite list of relators, each a word in the letters $x_i^{\pm 1}$. -/
  relators : List (List (ℕ × Bool))
  /-- Every letter of every relator refers to one of the generators. -/
  index_lt : ∀ w ∈ relators, ∀ l ∈ w, l.1 < numGenerators

namespace FinitePresentation

/-- A finite presentation is the same thing as a pair `(n, R)` in which every letter of every
word of `R` has index less than `n`. -/
def equivSubtype :
    FinitePresentation ≃
      {p : ℕ × List (List (ℕ × Bool)) // ∀ w ∈ p.2, ∀ l ∈ w, l.1 < p.1} where
  toFun P := ⟨(P.numGenerators, P.relators), P.index_lt⟩
  invFun p := ⟨p.1.1, p.1.2, p.2⟩
  left_inv _ := rfl
  right_inv _ := rfl

open Primrec in
/-- The condition that every letter of every word has index less than `n` is primitive
recursive. -/
theorem primrecPred_index_lt :
    PrimrecPred fun p : ℕ × List (List (ℕ × Bool)) =>
      ∀ w ∈ p.2, ∀ l ∈ w, l.1 < p.1 := by
  have hh : Primrec₂ fun (p : ℕ × List (List (ℕ × Bool))) (ls : (ℕ × Bool) × Bool) =>
      (decide (ls.1.1 < p.1) && ls.2) :=
    to₂ <| Primrec.and.comp
      ((nat_lt.comp (fst.comp (fst.comp snd)) (fst.comp fst)).decide) (snd.comp snd)
  refine (Primrec.eq.comp (list_foldr (list_flatten.comp snd) (const true) hh)
    (const true)).of_eq fun p => ?_
  rw [← List.forall_mem_flatten]
  induction p.2.flatten with
  | nil => simp
  | cons l L ih => simp [ih]

/-- Finite presentations are finite data, so they can be fed to algorithms. -/
instance : Primcodable FinitePresentation :=
  @Primcodable.ofEquiv _ _ (Primcodable.subtype primrecPred_index_lt) equivSubtype

/-- The relators of `P`, as elements of the free group on the generators
$x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$. -/
def relatorSet (P : FinitePresentation) : Set (FreeGroup (Fin P.numGenerators)) :=
  {r | ∃ (w : List (ℕ × Bool)) (hw : w ∈ P.relators),
    r = FreeGroup.mk (w.pmap (fun l hl => (⟨l.1, hl⟩, l.2)) (P.index_lt w hw))}

/-- The group $\langle x_0, \dots, x_{n-1} \mid R \rangle$ presented by `P`. -/
abbrev PresentedGroup (P : FinitePresentation) : Type :=
  _root_.PresentedGroup P.relatorSet

end FinitePresentation

/-- A group has finite (Prüfer) rank if there is an integer $r$ such that every finitely
generated subgroup can be generated by $r$ elements. -/
def HasFiniteRank (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ r : ℕ, ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG →
    ∃ S : Finset G, S.card ≤ r ∧ Subgroup.closure (S : Set G) = H

/--
Is the isomorphism problem soluble for finitely presented soluble groups of finite rank?

That is, is there an algorithm which, given two finite presentations $P$ and $Q$ of soluble
groups of finite rank, halts with the answer `true` if the groups presented by $P$ and $Q$
are isomorphic and with the answer `false` otherwise? When $P$ or $Q$ does not present a
soluble group of finite rank, the algorithm may answer arbitrarily or fail to halt.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.53» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ f : FinitePresentation → FinitePresentation →. Bool, Partrec₂ f ∧
      ∀ P Q : FinitePresentation,
        IsSolvable P.PresentedGroup → HasFiniteRank P.PresentedGroup →
        IsSolvable Q.PresentedGroup → HasFiniteRank Q.PresentedGroup →
        ∃ b ∈ f P Q, (b = true ↔ Nonempty (P.PresentedGroup ≃* Q.PresentedGroup)) := by
  sorry

/-- The trivial group has finite rank. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem hasFiniteRank_of_subsingleton (G : Type*) [Group G] [Subsingleton G] :
    HasFiniteRank G := by
  refine ⟨0, fun H _ => ⟨∅, le_rfl, ?_⟩⟩
  rw [Finset.coe_empty, Subgroup.closure_empty]
  exact Subsingleton.elim _ _

/-- A presentation without generators presents the trivial group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem subsingleton_presentedGroup_of_numGenerators_eq_zero (P : FinitePresentation)
    (h : P.numGenerators = 0) : Subsingleton P.PresentedGroup := by
  have : IsEmpty (Fin P.numGenerators) := by rw [h]; infer_instance
  refine ⟨fun a b => ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := PresentedGroup.mk_surjective _ a
  obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := PresentedGroup.mk_surjective _ b
  rw [Subsingleton.elim x y]

end Kourovka.«9.53»
attempts.decomposition_objections: Minor: the notes describe the algorithm as a 'computable predicate on pairs of encoded finite presentations' (suggesting a total function) while also saying behaviour outside the class is 'unconstrained'. These are not equivalent in general (a partial algorithm correct on the class need not have a total computable extension, since the class is neither c.e. nor co-c.e.). I followed the 'unconstrained' reading and the literature's usage by allowing a partial recursive algorithm that must halt only on the promise set; a reviewer preferring the total reading should replace `→. Bool, Partrec₂ f` by `→ Bool, Computable₂ f` and `∃ b ∈ f P Q, (b = true ↔ …)` by `(f P Q = true ↔ …)`.
modeling_decisions: 'Soluble isomorphism problem' is modelled as a promise problem with a PARTIAL recursive function (Partrec₂): on pairs of presentations that both present soluble groups of finite rank, f must halt and output true iff the groups are isomorphic; outside the promise f may output anything or fail to halt. This follows standard promise-problem semantics and matches how such algorithms are given in the literature (e.g. Segal's algorithm for polycyclic-by-finite groups does not halt on other inputs). A total Computable₂ version would be a stronger statement, not provably equivalent since the class is neither c.e. nor co-c.e.

'Finite rank' is Prüfer/Mal'cev rank: ∃ r, ∀ finitely generated subgroup H, ∃ S : Finset G with S.card ≤ r and Subgroup.closure S = H (as in the decomposition notes; equals finite abelian section rank / minimax for f.g. soluble groups).

A finite presentation is encoded as (n, list of relator words over ℕ × Bool) with the well-formedness condition that all indices are < n; the letter (i, true) is x_i and (i, false) is x_i⁻¹ (Mathlib's FreeGroup.mk convention). Relators form a List (order/repetition irrelevant to the group).
Isomorphism is Nonempty (P.PresentedGroup ≃* Q.PresentedGroup); 'soluble group' is Mathlib's IsSolvable.
The promise is imposed on P and Q separately (each presents a soluble group of finite rank), and the pair is passed to the algorithm; nothing is assumed about the polycyclic-by-finite case.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.53

by D. J. S. Robinson

Is the isomorphism problem soluble for finitely presented soluble groups of finite rank?

Here a group has *finite rank* (finite Prüfer rank, also called finite special rank) if there
is an integer $r$ such that every finitely generated subgroup can be generated by at most $r$
elements. For finitely generated soluble groups this is equivalent to having finite abelian
section rank and to being minimax.

The isomorphism problem is *soluble* for a class $\mathfrak{X}$ of finitely presented groups if
there is an algorithm which, given two finite presentations of groups in $\mathfrak{X}$,
decides whether the presented groups are isomorphic. Since membership in $\mathfrak{X}$ is not
itself required to be decidable, this is a promise problem: the behaviour of the algorithm on
presentations of groups outside $\mathfrak{X}$ is unconstrained.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.53»

/-- A group $G$ has finite (Prüfer) rank if there is $r \in \mathbb{N}$ such that every finitely
generated subgroup of $G$ can be generated by at most $r$ elements. -/
def HasFiniteRank (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ r : ℕ, ∀ (H : Subgroup G) [Group.FG H], Group.rank H ≤ r

/-- A finite group has finite rank. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem hasFiniteRank_of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] : HasFiniteRank G := by
  classical
  refine ⟨Nat.card G, fun H _ => ?_⟩
  have : Fintype H := Fintype.ofFinite H
  calc Group.rank H ≤ (Finset.univ : Finset H).card := Group.rank_le (by simp)
    _ = Nat.card H := by simp [Nat.card_eq_fintype_card]
    _ ≤ Nat.card G := Subgroup.card_le_card_group H

/-- A cyclic group has finite rank. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem hasFiniteRank_of_isCyclic (G : Type*) [Group G] [IsCyclic G] : HasFiniteRank G := by
  refine ⟨1, fun H _ => ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := isCyclic_iff_exists_zpowers_eq_top.mp (inferInstanceAs (IsCyclic H))
  calc Group.rank H ≤ ({g} : Finset H).card :=
        Group.rank_le (by rw [Finset.coe_singleton, ← Subgroup.zpowers_eq_closure, hg])
    _ = 1 := Finset.card_singleton g

/-- A finite presentation of a group: a number `numGenerators` of generators together with a
finite list of relators, each relator being a word in the generators and their inverses. A
letter `(i, b)` stands for the generator with index `i` if `b = true` and for its inverse
if `b = false`. Letters with index `≥ numGenerators` are ignored (they are read as the
identity), so that every list encodes a finite presentation and every finite presentation on
`numGenerators` generators is encoded. -/
structure FinitePresentation where
  /-- The number of generators. -/
  numGenerators : ℕ
  /-- The relators, as words in the letters `(i, b)`. -/
  relators : List (List (ℕ × Bool))

/-- Finite presentations are encoded as pairs `(numGenerators, relators)`; this is the
encoding with respect to which algorithms are required to be computable. -/
instance : Primcodable FinitePresentation :=
  .ofEquiv (ℕ × List (List (ℕ × Bool)))
    { toFun := fun P => (P.numGenerators, P.relators)
      invFun := fun p => ⟨p.1, p.2⟩
      left_inv := fun _ => rfl
      right_inv := fun _ => rfl }

/-- The element of the free group on `Fin n` read from a word in the letters `(i, b)`;
letters with `n ≤ i` are read as the identity. -/
def FinitePresentation.toFreeGroup (n : ℕ) (w : List (ℕ × Bool)) : FreeGroup (Fin n) :=
  FreeGroup.lift (fun i => if h : i < n then FreeGroup.of (⟨i, h⟩ : Fin n) else 1)
    (FreeGroup.mk w)

/-- The group defined by a finite presentation `P`: the quotient of the free group on
`P.numGenerators` generators by the normal closure of the relators of `P`. -/
abbrev FinitePresentation.group (P : FinitePresentation) : Type :=
  PresentedGroup {r | r ∈ P.relators.map (FinitePresentation.toFreeGroup P.numGenerators)}

theorem FinitePresentation.group_fg (P : FinitePresentation) : Group.FG P.group :=
  have : Group.FG (FreeGroup (Fin P.numGenerators)) :=
    Group.fg_iff.mpr ⟨Set.range FreeGroup.of, FreeGroup.closure_range_of _, Set.finite_range _⟩
